chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the male slave and the female slave: do they prevent (inheritors from inheriting) if they do not inherit? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.إِذَا لَمْ يَرِثَا: If they do not inherit (dual form)

ai.seo_question: Do slaves prevent other heirs from inheriting in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific mechanism of 'hajb' (exclusion) by slaves, ruling that they do not exclude other heirs unless they themselves are entitled to inherit. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the status of the *abd* (slave) from free heirs, noting that while a slave may inherit, their share is often subject to different conditions or deductions compared to free relatives. The hadith underscores the precision of Imami legal reasoning in distinguishing between the capacity to inherit and the power to exclude others from the estate.
